pointers.sentence: The 6.0 notes give it as a defence against content injection, such as cross-site scripting (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
The **nonce** is a value new for every request, which a policy that names it requires of an inline script or style (`docs/ref/csp.txt`).

The enumeration `CSP` holds the specification's quoted keywords, such as `CSP.SELF`, and one placeholder of Django's own, `CSP.NONCE`, which stands in a policy for the request's nonce (`django/utils/csp.py:CSP`).

On the way out it writes each header whose policy is not empty and which the response lacks (`django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware`; [Content Security Policy: `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware` and the nonce](../security/csp.md)).
The context processor `django.template.context_processors.csp` gives a template the nonce as `"csp_nonce"` (`django/template/context_processors.py:csp`).
The decorators `csp_override` and `csp_report_only_override` give one view a policy of its own (`django/views/decorators/csp.py:_make_csp_decorator`).

Both settings are empty by default (`django/conf/global_settings.py`), and the settings startproject writes name neither the middleware nor the processor (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`).

Both settings are empty by default (`django/conf/global_settings.py`), and the settings startproject writes name neither the middleware nor the processor (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`).
Given a form's media, it writes the media's tags, with the nonce if there is one (`django/utils/csp.py:nonce_attr`; [The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md)).
The admin's templates, admindocs' and the CSRF failure page carry the tag on their `<script>`, `<style>` and `<link>` elements (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
When the project has no `"403_csrf.html"`, the view `csrf_failure` renders the built-in `"csrf_403.html"` with an `Engine` of its own, and adds the nonce itself (`django/views/csrf.py:csrf_failure`).
Under 6.0.8 the element has no nonce, so a browser would refuse it (`docs/ref/csp.txt`).
It is registered without `deploy=True`, so check reports it without --deploy (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_csp_nonce_context_processor`; [The security checks](../security/checks.md)).

So the cookie "draft" with the salt "s" and the cookie "drafts" with none made the same salt, and a value signed for either was accepted for the other (CVE-2026-6873, `docs/releases/5.2.15.txt`; [Security fixes: disclosure, spoofing and privilege](security-fixes-exposure.md)).

`HttpResponseBase.set_signed_cookie` now signs with a salt of a fixed prefix, the length of the caller's salt, that salt and the name, so that no two pairs of name and salt make one string (`django/core/signing.py:_cookie_signer_salt`).
When it is true and the new salt fails for any reason but age, the function `_unsign_cookie` tries the old one (`django/core/signing.py:_unsign_cookie`).
The 6.1 notes list "Signed cookies now use an unambiguous salt derivation by default" among its features (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
What `set_signed_cookie("draft", "4", salt="s")` wrote then was signed with the same old salt, "drafts" (`django/core/signing.py:_cookie_signer_legacy_salt`).
Since 6.1 a project that sets the fallback gets a warning, whatever the value (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

Since 6.1, at the default, `HttpRequest.get_signed_cookie` treats it as a forged one: it raises `BadSignature`, or returns the default it was given (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_signed_cookie`).
A call that names no algorithm warns since 6.1, whether to `salted_hmac`, the keyed hash under Django's signing, or to `base64_hmac`, with which `Signer` signs (`django/core/signing.py:base64_hmac`).

Django's own callers name the algorithm, so signing never meets the warning: `Signer` names the one it was made with, SHA-256 by default (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`; [Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](../security/keys.md), [Signing: `Signer`, `TimestampSigner`, `dumps` and `loads`](../security/signing.md)).
`Signer` takes keyword arguments only since 5.1, which removed the positional ones deprecated in 4.2 (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`).
`TimestampSigner` inherits the same `__init__` (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.__init__`).
It came in 4.1, when `CsrfViewMiddleware` stopped masking the secret in its cookie, to keep the cookie masked while a project's instances were upgraded (`docs/releases/4.1.txt`).
Under all four a project that still sets it true gets, without a warning, a cookie of 32 characters, the secret itself (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._set_csrf_cookie`).

A cookie of 64 characters, a masked secret, is still accepted, and unmasked as it is read (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._get_secret`; [The CSRF secret and its token](../security/csrf-token.md)).
